headline: Physics-based simulation and scoring applied to binding, coarse-graining and hotspots
label: Physics Based Molecular Modelling
summary: Recent preprints and papers benchmark free energy methods and extend coarse-grained and fragment-based physics models to structural questions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit physical description, through free energy perturbation, molecular dynamics, coarse-grained force fields or fragment molecular orbital calculations, used to improve sampling, scoring or interpretation of biomolecular structure and binding. Four preprints benchmark relative binding free energy engines (Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, BLaDE-MSLD) on shared Amber force fields. The AB-FEP integrin study and the Fc-FcRn variant work apply perturbation methods to ligand conformational preference and antibody binding energetics, the latter with coupling and conformational corrections. MARTINI2 is integrated into HADDOCK3 for large complexes, and Martini Mapper automates Martini 3 model construction from SMILES. Newer elements include high-pressure MD used to flag fragile AlphaFold3 regions, MD-derived pharmacophore signatures for protein-peptide interfaces, and FMOPhore's fragment orbital hotspot classification. The items differ in scope, but each relies on an explicit physical model.
